summary.title: 12 "Manager READMEs" from Silicon Valley's Top Tech Companies
summary.one_liner: A roundup of twelve public "Manager README" documents from engineering leaders at companies like Slack, Netflix, Shopify and HubSpot, plus the sections they commonly include and how to roll one out to a team.
keywords: how to write a manager readme
takeaways: A Manager README is a short document where a manager explains their working style, values, 1:1 format, feedback preferences and calendar habits to their team.

Examples from Slack, Netflix, Shopify, Forter, InVision, HubSpot, Etsy, Stratasan, Rent the Runway, Unity, BiblioCommons and others show varied styles, from personal quirks to response-time expectations.
Common sections include What is this, About Me, Personal Principles, One-on-Ones, Feedback, and How to interpret my calendar; some add performance scales and the DRI principle.
The author suggests delivering the README in a 1:1 and starting during onboarding, or when inheriting a team.
summary.summary: The article is a curated collection of twelve publicly shared Manager README documents from engineering managers and leads at well-known tech companies. For each example, the author lists favourite parts with links to the original documents, which are often hosted as Google Docs, GitHub files, or blog posts. It then summarises the sections most READMEs share, such as 1:1 cadence, feedback preferences, and calendar guidance, and some optional ones like performance scales and the DRI principle. The piece closes with advice on rolling the document out in a one-on-one during onboarding, written by the CEO of SoapBox, a promotional tool for manager 1:1s.
